For a long time, the idea that we would have A.I.s or robots that we could talk to, interact with, integrate into our personal lives — that was fantasy, science fiction. But now, talking to A.I. systems is mainstream. Roughly half of American adults are using chatbots. Many of them are going pretty deep with their A.I.s. Nearly one in five U.S. adults has chatted with an A.I. that simulates a romantic partner. The results here can get dark. Google’s own researchers have found that some children are now struggling to distinguish between talking with chatbots and interacting with humans. Since the 1970s, the sociologist Sherry Turkle has been studying the relationships between humans and machines. In the ’80s, she predicted that computers would evolve into these second selves. I think that basically came true — think of the smartphone in your pocket that you’re always looking at. In 2011, just a year after Instagram came out, Turkle warned that social media might create a society where, even though we’re constantly talking to one another, we’re in this strange state of being alone together.
